summary: PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23 is a careful extraction of arXiv v2 of Chang–Chen–Mishiba (Forum Math. Pi 2023): 51 items, 2 routes and 4 source issues. The main statements hold up against both the preprint and the version of record. The 4 source issues and the dual locators check out. The dimension counts |I^T_w| = |IND_w| = d'_w hold for q ≤ 9 and w ≤ 16, and Chen's formula (with the corrected (q − 1) | j), Carlitz's identity and Thakur's relation R_1 were verified by exact computation. There are 10 findings: 5 medium and 5 low. Medium: (1) Section 5's analytic apparatus has no item. This covers Ω, π̃ := 1/Ω(θ), the deformation series 𝓛(s) ∈ E and its specialisation, the matrices of the key lemma, Papanikolas §4.1.6, CPY Prop. 2.2.1, and π̃ ∈ (−θ)^{1/(q−1)}k_∞^×. Item 51 misplaces it in §1.3 as unreproved, and the DM.8 packet requests a different sign normalisation. (2) Theorem 5.2.1 uses π̃^w ∈ Z_w for (q − 1) | w, which is Carlitz's evaluation of ζ_A(n); it has no item, and item 4 is marked planned at DM.6, which plans only Taelman's formula. (3) The accepted DM.8 source route (the ABP criterion, E, twisting) never reached the DM.8 blueprint issue #1009. The DM.8 packet of 27 September neither cites the paper nor plans the criterion, yet the Part II brief imports them from DM.8. (4) Seven of the 12 prerequisite links resolve to unrelated papers (Lévy processes, tumour cells, Casimir energy, …), and Todd, H.-J. Chen and Chang–Mishiba are misnamed. (5) A missed misprint in Corollary 1.2.7 (Z_{v,w} a k̄-space bounded in dim_k), copied into item 12, whose statement is therefore false as written. Low: two further surviving cross-reference misprints, one of which the review wrongly dismissed as preprint-only; item 1 and item 30 miss Mathlib's RatFunc.inftyValuation/CompletionAtInfty and PowerSeries.IsRestricted; item 2 cites FA.0, which plans no C_∞; the appendix maps ℬ, 𝒞, ℬ𝒞, U_1–U_3, Init and the published Remark 5.4 have no items; and there is no sourceVersions, so data/collation.json misfiles the paper as preprint-only.

Computations. |I^T_w| = |IND_w| = d'_w for q ∈ {2,3,4,5,7,8,9} and 1 ≤ w ≤ 16. IND°_w lists for q = 3, w ≤ 8, and Example 4.3.2's IND°_q = {(1, q−1)} and IND°_{2q−2} = {(q−1,q−1),(2q−2)}. The v-adic bound d'_w − d'_{w−(q−1)} for q = 3, 4. These were computed by enumerating compositions. By exact arithmetic in F_p(θ): H.-J. Chen's formula (2.3.2) with the corrected condition (q − 1) | j holds for q ∈ {2,3}, d ∈ {0,1,2}, 1 ≤ s,n ≤ 4 (96 cases, no failure). Carlitz's identity 1/L_d^s = Σ_{a∈A_{+,d}} a^{−s} holds for s ≤ q and fails at s = q + 1, d ≥ 1. Thakur's relation ℒ^ζ_d(q) = L_1 ℒ^ζ_{d+1}(1, q−1) (the binary relation R_1) holds for q ∈ {2,3}, d ≤ 2. Remark 2.3.4 was checked by hand: the only admissible j is q − 1 with s + n = q, and the binomial terms cancel, since 2 = 0 when q is even.

findings.where: PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23 items /51, /17, /39, /40 and the route 1 brief; report section 'The routes'
findings.claim: The analytic apparatus of Section 5, on which the independence half actually runs, has no item. Item 51 locates it only in the §1.3 strategy sketch (step II-1) and says the paper 'deliberately does not reprove' it. In fact the paper sets up and uses these objects explicitly. (a) Ω(t) := (−θ)^{−q/(q−1)} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − t/θ^{q^i}), with Ω^{(−1)} = (t − θ)Ω, Ω ∈ E, and the normalisation π̃ := 1/Ω(θ). (b) The polynomials 𝕃_0 = 1, 𝕃_d = (t − θ^q)⋯(t − θ^{q^d}), and the deformation series 𝓛(s) := Ω^{wt(s)} Σ_{d_1>⋯>d_r≥0} 1/(𝕃_{d_1}^{s_1}⋯𝕃_{d_r}^{s_r}). It lies in 𝕋 and in E by [9, Lemma 5.3.1], and specialises as 𝓛(s)|_{t=θ^{q^j}} = (Li_s(1)/π̃^{wt(s)})^{q^j} for j ≥ 0 by [14, Prop. 2.3.3]. (c) The matrices Φ′, Ψ′, Φ, Ψ, the extended Φ̃ and the vector ψ built from them in the proof of Lemma 5.1.1, which satisfy Ψ^{(−1)} = ΦΨ and ψ^{(−1)} = Φ̃ψ by [14, (2.3.4), (2.3.7)]. (d) Three facts the proof invokes: uniqueness of solutions X^{(−1)} = diag(Φ′,1)X up to GL(F_q(t)) [27, §4.1.6]; the common-denominator statement [14, Prop. 2.2.1] used in part (2); and π̃ ∈ (−θ)^{1/(q−1)}·k_∞^×, which is what turns 'Σ a Li(1) ∈ k·π̃^{w−wt(s)}' into the dichotomy 'vanishes or (q − 1) | (w − wt(s))' of part (1). The joined Part II extractions carry exactly these objects: PAPER-NGODAC-21/omega, /L-series, /L-theta, /period-power, /trivialization-uniqueness, /constant-denominator, and PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/omega-and-carlitz-period, /pi-power-outside-Fqbar-laurent. This extraction, whose Lemma 5.1.1 is stated for arbitrary M rather than depth two, does not. The normalisation also needs pinning: the DM.8 packet requests from DM.2 'π̃ = −1/Ω(θ)', while this paper sets π̃ := 1/Ω(θ). The key lemma's conclusions Li_P(1) ∈ k·π̃^w and the specialisation formula depend on that choice (only up to F_q^×, but a formal statement must fix one).
findings.evidence: Published text (Forum Math. Pi 11 (2023) e26), §5, pp. 21–22: 'Following [2], we consider the following power series: Ω(t) := (−θ)^{−q/(q−1)} ∏_{i=1}^∞ (1 − t/θ^{q^i}) … it satisfies … Ω^{(−1)}(t) = (t − θ)Ω(t). In addition, we have Ω(t) ∈ E and π̃ := 1/Ω(θ) is the fundamental period of the Carlitz module … we define the following deformation series: 𝓛(s) := Ω^{wt(s)} Σ 1/(𝕃^{s_1}_{d_1}⋯𝕃^{s_r}_{d_r}) ∈ 𝕋 … It is shown in [9, Lemma 5.3.1] that 𝓛(s) ∈ E. Moreover, by [14, Proposition 2.3.3], we have 𝓛(s)|_{t=θ^{q^j}} = (Li_s(1)/π̃^{wt(s)})^{q^j}' (arXiv v2 p. 21–22, same text). Proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 22–24: 'We define matrices Φ′ … and Ψ′ …'; 'Then using [14, (2.3.4), (2.3.7)], one checks that Ψ^{(−1)} = ΦΨ and ψ^{(−1)} = Φψ'; 'Thus, by [27, §4.1.6], Ψ … GL(F_q(t)) …'; 'the first statement of (1) follows from this relation because π̃ ∈ (−θ)^{1/(q−1)}·k_∞^×'; '(2) By (5.2) and [14, Proposition 2.2.1], there exists α ∈ F_q[t] \ {0} such that αg ∈ Mat(k̄[t])' (arXiv v2 p. 24 cites [Pap08, §4.1.6] and [CPY19, Proposition 2.2.1]). Item 51 note: 'This is the input the paper deliberately does not reprove'; item 51 locator 'Section 1.3, step (II-1)'. Packet DrinfeldModulesAndTModules--DM.8, requests[0]: 'compatible period normalization π̃=−1/Ω(θ)'.
findings.fix: Add items, routed to the Part II (or, for the general facts, to DM.2/DM.8 via the source route), with the paper's locators (Section 5 preamble; proof of Lemma 5.1.1 = published Lemma 5.1): (i) Ω(t), its difference equation, Ω ∈ E, and π̃ := 1/Ω(θ) with the remark that DM.8's request uses −1/Ω(θ); (ii) 𝕃_d and the deformation series 𝓛(s) ∈ 𝕋 ∩ E with its specialisation at t = θ^{q^j} (after Chang [9, Lemma 5.3.1] and Chang–Papanikolas–Yu [14, Prop. 2.3.3]); (iii) the Frobenius system satisfied by (𝓛(n))_{n ∈ 𝓘(s)} and the matrices Φ′, Ψ′, Φ, Ψ, Φ̃, ψ of the key lemma's proof; (iv) π̃ ∈ (−θ)^{1/(q−1)} k_∞^×, hence π̃^n ∈ k_∞ iff (q − 1) | n; (v) Papanikolas §4.1.6 (fundamental matrices unique up to GL(F_q(t))) and [14, Prop. 2.2.1], cited to DM.8. Rewrite item 51 so that its locator is §1.3 (II-1) together with §5 and the proof of Lemma 5.1.1, and drop 'deliberately does not reprove': Remark 1.3.2 omits only the construction of the dual t-motives, and the matrices are written out in the proof. Carry (i)–(iv) into the route 1 brief's list of what the Part II must cover or import.

findings.where: PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23/4 (status planned at DM.0, DM.2, DM.6) and the proof of Theorem 5.2.1; route 1 brief ('Carlitz zeta values and Goss L-values from DM.6')
findings.claim: The proof of Theorem 5.2.1 (published Theorem 5.2), in the case (q − 1) | w, rests on 'π̃^w ∈ Z_w'. That is Carlitz's theorem: ζ_A(n)/π̃^n ∈ k^× when (q − 1) | n, with explicit Bernoulli–Carlitz coefficient. The paper uses it without comment, and it has no item. Item 4, which is supposed to carry the depth-one values, states no theorem at all ('whose exponential, period π̃ and logarithm control them'). It is marked planned at DM.0, DM.2 and DM.6, but none of them plans ζ_A(n) for n ≥ 2 or Carlitz's evaluation. DM.6 plans Taelman's class-number formula for Drinfeld modules. Its acceptance test 'The Carlitz module must recover its explicit zeta value' concerns the single value L(C/A, 1) = ζ_A(1). The reviewed library audit lists DM.6's targets as Taelman's L-value, unit lattice, class module, covolume and class-number formula only. So the depth-one input the independence proof needs is unplanned, and the planned status overclaims.
findings.evidence: Published p. 25 (arXiv v2 p. 25), proof of Theorem 5.2: 'When (q − 1) | w, we have π̃^w ∈ Z_w and hence Theorem 3.8 implies that there exists P_w … such that Supp(P_w) ⊂ I^ND_w and Li_{P_w}(1) = π̃^w.' Stage DrinfeldModulesAndTModules:DM.6 (atlas extract): 'For Taelman's integral Drinfeld-module setting … construct the convergent Euler-product value, exponential unit lattice, finite class module … Acceptance: The Carlitz module must recover its explicit zeta value and period normalization'. data/library-coverage.json, DrinfeldModulesAndTModules:DM.6 targets: Taelman's Euler-product L-value, U(φ/A) and the class module, covolume and Fitting polynomial, the nuclear-operator identity, Taelman's class-number formula. Item 4 statement: 'The depth-one values ζ_A(s) = Σ_{a ∈ A_+} a^{-s} are the Carlitz zeta values, attached to the Carlitz module C : t ↦ θ + τ, whose exponential, period π̃ and logarithm control them.' Compare PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/carlitz-zeta-q-minus-1 (only the case n = q − 1).
findings.fix: Split item 4. (a) A definition item, 'the Carlitz zeta values ζ_A(n) = Σ_{a∈A_+} a^{−n} ∈ k_∞, n ≥ 1', status missing, routed to the Part II as the depth-one case of item 3. (b) A theorem item, 'Carlitz: for n ≥ 1 with (q − 1) | n, ζ_A(n) = (BC_n/Π(n))·π̃^n with BC_n ∈ k the Bernoulli–Carlitz number and Π(n) the Carlitz factorial, so ζ_A(n) ∈ k^×·π̃^n; in particular π̃^w ∈ Z_w for (q − 1) | w'. Its locator is the proof of Theorem 5.2.1 (published Theorem 5.2), after Carlitz 1935 [8] and Thakur's book §5. It is missing and routed to DM.6 as a source (or to the Part II if DM.6's owner declines). Keep item 4's planned status only for the Carlitz module itself (DM.0) and its period (DM.2). Add 'Carlitz's evaluation at multiples of q − 1' to the route 1 brief's imports, naming its owner.

findings.claim: Seven of the twelve prerequisite links point to unrelated works, and three entries misname the paper or its author. The maintainer adds these to a later batch, so the wrong ids would bring in the wrong papers. (1) Chang, Compos. Math. 150 (2014): 'arXiv:1207.4736' is a paper on Lévy processes; the correct id is arXiv:1207.2326. (2) Ngo Dac, Ann. of Math. 194 (2021): 'arXiv:2007.11060' is 'On Log-Algebraic Identities for Anderson t-modules and Characteristic p Multiple Zeta Values'; use doi:10.4007/annals.2021.194.1.6 (public copy HAL hal-03298790, as PAPER-NGODAC-21 records). (3) Chang–Papanikolas–Yu, JEMS 21 (2019): 'arXiv:1601.01927' is a paper on circulating tumour-cell microfilters; the correct id is arXiv:1411.0124. (4) H.-J. Chen, JNT 148 (2015): 'doi:10.1016/j.jnt.2014.09.019' is Berndt–Kang–Sohn on Rogers–Ramanujan continued fractions; the correct DOI is 10.1016/j.jnt.2014.09.016, and the author is Huei-Jeng Chen, not 'Hsin-Jui Chen'. (5) Chang–Mishiba: the paper's [13] is 'On a conjecture of Furusho over function fields', Invent. Math. 223 (2021), 49–102 (doi:10.1007/s00222-020-00988-1, arXiv:1710.10849), not 'On finite Carlitz multiple polylogarithms / v-adic multiple zeta values'; and 'arXiv:1908.06398' is a paper on stochastic orders. (6) Lara Rodríguez–Thakur: 'arXiv:1401.2708' is a paper on Casimir energy; the correct id is arXiv:1312.4928 (doi:10.1007/s13226-014-0089-0). (7) Todd: the author is George Todd, not 'Robert Todd'; 'doi:10.1016/j.jnt.2017.10.025' is Oppenheim–Shusterman, 'Squarefree polynomials with prescribed coefficients'; the correct DOI is 10.1016/j.jnt.2017.09.028. In addition, the Thakur entry names a non-existent 'Multizeta values for F_q[t], relations and conjectures (2017)'; the paper's [35] is 'Multizeta values for function fields: a survey', J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 29 (2017). It also attributes the basic binary relation to the listed Thakur works, while the paper cites [33] 'Relations between multizeta values for F_q[t]', IMRN 2009 (doi:10.1093/imrn/rnp018), Thm. 5, which is not listed.

findings.where: PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23/12 (Corollary 1.2.7 = published Corollary 1.8) and PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23 sourceIssues (a missed misprint)
findings.claim: Corollary 1.2.7 is printed with two slips, and item 12 copies the substantive one, so the item's statement is false as written. The paper defines Z_{v,w} as 'the k̄-vector space space by v-adic MZV's of weight w' and bounds 'dim_k Z_{v,w}'. A nonzero k̄-vector space has infinite dimension over k, so the inequality fails whenever Z_{v,w} ≠ 0. The argument the paper gives supports the k-reading. By [13, Thm. 1.2.2] there is a natural k-linear map from ∞-adic to v-adic MZVs; by [11] it is an algebra map, and its kernel contains ζ_A(q − 1)·Z_{w−(q−1)} because ζ_A(q − 1)_v = 0 [19]. Multiplication by ζ_A(q − 1) ≠ 0 is injective and maps Z_{w−(q−1)} into Z_w (q-shuffle), so dim_k of the k-span of v-adic MZVs of weight w is at most d'_w − d'_{w−(q−1)}. (The k̄-reading with dim_{k̄} also holds, via Remark 1.2.6, but mixing the two is wrong.) 'space space' should read 'spanned'. The extraction found and recorded the neighbouring 'dim_w' slip (E3) but not this one, and neither did the review.
findings.evidence: arXiv v2 source (Basis_Submit_v2.tex, line 443) and p. 4: 'we let \cZ_{v,w} be the \ok-vector space space by v-adic MZV's of weight w defined in~\cite{CM21}. Then we have \dim_{k} \cZ_{v,w}\leq d_{w}'-d_{w-(q-1)}''. Published p. 4, Corollary 1.8 (checked on the page image): 'we let Z_{v,w} be the k̄-vector space space by v-adic MZV's of weight w defined in [13]. Then we have dim_k Z_{v,w} ≤ d'_w − d'_{w−(q−1)}'. Published p. 4, the sentence before: 'By [13, Thm. 1.2.2], there is a natural k-linear map from (∞-adic) MZV's to v-adic MZV's, and it was further shown in [11] that the map is indeed an algebra homomorphism with kernel containing the ideal generated by ζ_A(q − 1) since ζ_A(q − 1)_v = 0 by [19].' Item 12 statement: 'let Z_{v,w} be the k̄-vector space spanned by the v-adic MZVs of weight w. Then dim_k Z_{v,w} ≤ d'_w − d'_{w-(q-1)}'.

Item 30 says the Tate algebra 𝕋 is 'not constructed in the atlas'. Mathlib has restricted power series: PowerSeries.IsRestricted, and MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring over an ultrametric normed ring. With c = 1 this is 𝕋 once a normed C_∞ exists. findings.claim: The extraction read both the arXiv v2 source and the published text: its `source.read` says so, and E1–E4 were each compared with the Cambridge Core text. But it declares no `sourceVersions` (PROTOCOL §18), so collation.py falls back on the sourceIssues' free text. There the publisher is named only as 'doi:10.1017/fmp.2023.26' and 'Cambridge Core', which do not match PUBLISHER, whose pattern requires 'doi.org/10.' or 'cambridge.org'. 'arXiv' matches PREPRINT, so data/collation.json records the paper as read from the 'preprint'. Nothing is exposed today, since no finding has affects 'a stated result'. The new E5 (finding 5) does, and check_errata.py will then require sourceVersions. The published PDF served on 30 September 2026 was 25 pages, 'Received: 29 July 2022; Revised: 5 January 2023; Accepted: 5 September 2023'. A word-level collation against v2 shows only presentational differences plus the added Remark 5.4.
